rationale: Both describe gifts or sacrifices unable to perfect the worshiper. The earlier unit explicitly concerns conscience; here the law is a shadow and repeated yearly sacrifices cannot perfect those approaching. The particular images and stated effects remain distinct.

The earlier statement that gifts and sacrifices cannot perfect conscience explains the subject beside this rhetorical question about offerings ceasing after definitive cleansing. The question is not rewritten as an assertion that the offerings actually ceased.

The annual atonement statute provides a concrete year-by-year sacrificial setting beside the reminder of sins year by year. The statute and Hebrews assessment of repeated reminders retain their different statements.

relationship: animal blood and its stated limits
rationale: Both name animal blood in discussing purification. The earlier unit describes flesh-related cleansing, while this unit denies taking sins away by bulls and goats. The different objects and effects are kept rather than presenting them as identical claims.

relationship: quotation with body and ears difference
rationale: The sacrifice-and-offering rejection corresponds to Psalm39:7. Hebrews then says a body was prepared; the supplied Psalm says ears were prepared and also mentions burnt and sin offerings. The actual body/ears difference is preserved.

The burnt-offering and sin-offering saying corresponds to the latter part of Psalm39:7. Hebrews speaks of taking no pleasure, while the Psalm says not requested. The verbs and the Psalms additional ears clause remain distinct.

The scroll-of-the-book, coming and doing-Gods-will clauses correspond to these two Psalm units. The Psalm says I desired to do Thy will and adds law within the belly; Hebrews presents coming to do the will. The wording and boundaries remain as printed.

This summarizes the earlier sacrifice, offering, burnt-offering and sin-offering saying found in Psalm39:7. Hebrews adds its offered-according-to-law explanation; that explanation is not inserted into the Psalm unit.

relationship: first and second statements in context
rationale: The earlier quoted statements provide the sequence behind He then said and the first/second contrast. Sacrificial non-desire precedes coming to do Gods will. The reference does not substitute an unprinted universal definition for first and second.

Both describe a decisive self-related offering rather than an endless sequence. The earlier unit says He offered Himself once for all; this names the body of Jesus Christ and sanctification by that will. The added predicates remain in their own units.

Daily standing and repeated priestly offerings are compared with the same chapters yearly sacrifices unable to perfect. Daily/yearly, standing and shadow language remain distinct descriptions within the shared repetition argument.

The seated-at-the-right-hand statement corresponds to the Psalm command to sit at the right hand. Hebrews adds the one sacrifice for sins for all time; the Psalm supplies Lord-to-my-Lord speech and enemies as footstool, without printing the whole sacrifice claim.

The waiting-until-enemies-become-footstool clause directly corresponds to the Psalm right-hand saying. The source continues the preceding seated-sacrificer account; the Psalm does not itself give that whole sacrificial context.

Both connect the one offering with sanctification. The earlier unit says we have been sanctified through Jesus body once for all; here one offering perfects for all time those being sanctified. The actual verbal forms are not collapsed.

The following covenant-law and non-remembrance sayings supply the testimony introduced here. The introduction attributes testimony to the Holy Spirit; the following units preserve their own Lord-says and He-adds wording without naming an unprinted human author.

The laws-and-inward-inscription covenant promise corresponds to native Greek-based Jeremiah38:33. The exact heart/mind placement, pronouns and covenant recipients must remain in each supplied text; the reference does not silently make all wording identical.

The promise not to remember sins corresponds to the end of Jeremiah38:34. Hebrews also names lawless deeds; Jeremiah supplies its own surrounding knowledge and mercy clauses. Neither selected unit is completed with unprinted clauses from the other.

The foregoing non-remembrance promise is the immediate premise for the conclusion about forgiveness and no further sin offering. The pair follows the internal argument without turning the target promise into the exact words of the resulting inference.

The earlier account of entry by His own blood gives a concrete counterpart for the readers confidence of entry in Jesus blood. The subjects and the earlier once/eternal-redemption description remain distinct.

Matthew narrates the sanctuary curtain torn in two; Hebrews names entry through the curtain and explicitly explains it as His flesh. The narrative does not itself print that flesh interpretation or identify every clause of the new and living way.

The earlier exhortation explicitly names Jesus as apostle and high priest of the confession. That priest title supplies a concrete comparison for the great priest here in the Jesus-blood context. The house-of-God clause and apostle title remain distinct.

The water-cleansing and renewed-heart promise supplies specific cleansing and heart images beside the sprinkled hearts and water-washed body. Ezekiels promise and Hebrews approach exhortation retain their different objects; no exclusive rite is inferred.

Sarahs considering the One who promised faithful gives a concrete same-letter counterpart to the Promisers faithfulness supporting steadfast hope. Sarahs conception circumstances are not transferred to the readers confession instruction.

Both connect love with action toward one another. Galatians says to serve one another through love; Hebrews calls for mutual consideration that stirs love and good works. Their exhortations and surrounding freedom discussion remain distinct.

Both call for mutual encouragement with a stated time emphasis. The earlier unit specifies each day during Today to resist hardening; this names gathering and the approaching day. Today and the approaching day are not treated as identical dates.

Numbers distinguishes an involuntary sin offering from the proud-handed rejection that brings exclusion. This supplies a concrete contrast beside deliberate sin after knowledge of truth and no remaining sacrifice. The covenant settings and stated penalties remain distinct.

Isaiahs fire-and-adversaries saying gives a specific counterpart to fire about to consume the adversaries. Hebrews adds fearful expectation of judgment; the prophetic setting and every surrounding statement are not made identical.

relationship: two or three witnesses in death sentence
rationale: Deuteronomy explicitly requires two or three witnesses for a death sentence rather than one. Hebrews recalls the Mosaic threshold in its warning argument. The original case setting and the later application are not collapsed.

Both warn about rejection after described religious benefits and name the Son. Chapter6 describes enlightenment, shared Spirit and falling away; here the warning names covenant blood, trampling and insulting the Spirit of grace. No unstated identity or final theory is imposed on the sanctified pronoun.

The vengeance-and-repayment saying corresponds to native Deuteronomy32:35. The exact first-person and timing formulations are retained rather than importing every word of one quotation into the other supplied unit.

The Lord-judging-His-people saying corresponds to Deuteronomy32:36. The target also contains its own account of His servants and their condition; Hebrews uses the saying within the preceding warning. This second pair adds no second source completion.

relationship: falling into the Lords hands contrast
rationale: Davids choice of falling into the Lords hands because of His mercies has a concrete phrase counterpart here. Hebrews stresses the fearfulness of falling into the living Gods hands. The different circumstances and attitudes remain a stated contrast.

Both refer to enlightenment as a prior religious benefit. Chapter6 names it among other experiences; here readers recall their earlier enlightened days and endurance of suffering. The reference does not identify every person or consequence as the same.

Corinthians describes apostles as a spectacle to the world, angels and human beings; Hebrews recalls public exposure to reproach and affliction. The different groups and the additional companionship clause are not made identical events.

The later instruction to remember prisoners as if bound with them supplies a concrete counterpart to sympathy with prisoners here. The actual prisoners wording is retained; no my-bonds variant is inserted or author identified from it.

The earlier confidence for entry in Jesus blood supplies a concrete basis beside the warning not to discard confidence. This verse adds great reward; the entry description and reward statement remain distinct.

Both connect persevering trust with receiving promised benefit. Chapter6 names faith and patience inheriting promises; this unit names endurance and doing Gods will to receive the promise. The verbs and scope retain their own forms.

The coming-without-delay saying corresponds to Habakkuk2:3. The prophetic unit speaks in its vision setting; Hebrews says the coming One and a very little while. The wording does not by itself identify every referent or calculate a date.

The righteous-living-by-faith and shrinking-back/displeasure language corresponds to Habakkuk2:4. The exact possessives and clause order remain in each actual text rather than assuming the two formulations are identical.

relationship: response to faith and drawing back contrast
rationale: The preceding faith/drawing-back quotation supplies the alternatives beside the writers we assertion. This unit names destruction and preservation of the soul; those consequences are not silently inserted into the preceding quotation.
